cards.text: Hosea, a prophet of the LORD, tells this one himself, and friend, it's a heavy one. His wife is loved by another man, and she's an adulteress. Then the LORD speaks to Hosea.

cards.question: Hosea's wife is loved by another man. What does the LORD tell Hosea to do about her?

answers.text: Go show love to her again
Let her go her own way
Send her back to her family

cards.text: AGAIN? After ALL that? Hosea, I'd have dropped a whole tray of cookies right there. But God isn't done. He tells Hosea exactly what kind of love this is.

cards.question: The LORD tells Hosea to love his wife the way the LORD loves the ___, even though they turn to other gods.

cards.text: And God says the Israelites love to offer raisin cakes to idols. Raisin cakes. To a STATUE. As a baker, I'm offended on behalf of every oven I've ever met.
So Hosea goes. He doesn't just ask her to come home. He buys her back.

cards.question: Hosea buys back his wife. What does he pay for her?

answers.text: Fifteen shekels of silver and barley
Thirty shekels of silver and wine
Ten shekels of gold and oil

cards.text: Fifteen shekels and barley. Me? Mother Miller pulled me out of a closing-sale bin for 25 cents. A QUARTER. Then Hosea sits his wife down and tells her how it's going to be.

cards.question: Hosea tells his wife she must live with him for many days. What must she not do?
Hosea asks this of his wife but promises nothing in return.

cards.text: Then Hosea turns to Israel, and that line comes back: many days. The Israelites must live many days without some things they're used to having.

cards.question: For many days, what will the Israelites live without?

cards.text: No king. No prince. No sacrifice, no sacred pillar, no ephod. The list just keeps going.

cards.question: During those many days, Israel will still have its idols.

cards.text: But Hosea isn't done. There's an afterward. Friend, I LOVE an afterward. My whole life since that junk drawer is one big afterward.

cards.question: After those many days, what will the people of Israel do?

answers.text: Return and seek the LORD their God
Choose a king from another nation
Stay far from the LORD for good

cards.question: Israel will seek the LORD their God and ___ their king.

cards.text: Hosea says, "They will come trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the last days." I know a little about being called out of the dark, friend. Goodness on the other side is worth every shaky step.

findings.problem: "Then Hosea turns to Israel" says Hosea now speaks to or about Israel as a new subject. Verse 4 opens with "For" and leaves open how it connects to verse 3. The text never says Hosea addresses Israel. "Some things they're used to having" also adds a description the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Verse 4 begins with "For", which ties Hosea's wife living many days without belonging to another to Israel living many days without king or idol. Verse 1 also sets up "Love her as the LORD loves the Israelites." No card helps the baker see that verses 2 to 3 picture verses 4 to 5. That link is the heart of the passage. It can be pointed out without adding a reason the text doesn't give, for example by noting that "many days" shows up for both.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Rain or sunshine" is close to silly, since many days without sunshine isn't believable. It's also a different kind of thing from "A king or a prince", which names leaders, not weather.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card lists everything in verse 4 except the idol and then says "The list just keeps going." That signals one more item is missing, which points the baker toward False on card 14 ("Israel will still have its idols").

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "The list just keeps going" overstates the text. After ephod, verse 4 has only one more item, idol. This line is narration, not one of Papa Dorin's jokes.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "Friend, I LOVE an afterward. My whole life since that junk drawer is one big afterward" tells the baker the afterward is a happy one. That rules out card 16's wrong answer "Stay far from the LORD for good" before the question is asked.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: David first shows up as the answer to card 17, and no card ever says simply who he is (for example, Israel's great king from long before). Card 17 can't say it without giving the answer away, so card 18 should.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Multiple choice is 5 of the 9 choice cards (2, 7, 9, 12, 16). Fill in the blank and true or false have only 2 each, so multiple choice dominates the stop.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The joke calls back to "Mother Miller" pulling him out of a closing-sale bin for 25 cents. The line explains the bin and the price, but not who Mother Miller is. The joke logic test only confirms that bakers know about the junk drawer from onboarding.
findings.question: Does onboarding introduce Mother Miller and the 25-cent bakery bin, so the callback lands without explanation? Or must every backstory detail outside the junk drawer be explained in the line the way drawer details are?
